observed_text:
The registered NSK example links Smearing 7 to Smearing 5: the convex rollers in Smearing 7 belong to the same spherical roller bearing shown in Smearing 5, so the bearing type is inherited from that earlier example [EV-I01-002]. For Smearing 7, NSK reports smearing of the rolling surfaces on those convex rollers and attributes that example to poor lubrication [EV-I01-002]. This is a manufacturer's case statement, not a project observation [EV-I01-002]. The general NSK context describes smearing as surface damage from a collection of small seizures between bearing components caused by oil film rupture and/or sliding, with possible causes including high speed and light load, sudden acceleration/deceleration, improper lubricant, and entry of water [EV-I01-002]. The caller-assigned rolling_element category does not establish the same damage or cause in the CWRU bearing: the source is a spherical roller bearing rather than a CWRU deep-groove ball bearing, and the rolling-element classification does not prove smearing or a lubrication cause [EV-I01-002]. The poor-lubrication spherical-roller-smearing scenario is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation or classifier inference [EV-I01-002].

Evidence limitations:
The source is a spherical roller bearing, not a CWRU deep-groove ball bearing; no transfer validation to CWRU artificial defects or aviation equipment is provided [EV-I01-002].
The rolling-element category does not establish smearing or a lubrication root cause, and no specific lubricant, quantity, or acceptance limit is established [EV-I01-002].
The smearing and poor-lubrication attribution is the manufacturer's reported example, not a project observation or sample fact [EV-I01-002].
The scenario's assumed cause is a teaching assumption, not an observation or classifier inference [EV-I01-002].
Evidence scope is registered generic bearing education only; no model-specific or aviation/reuse authorization is supplied [EV-I01-002].
